Folks — forwarding MidCity's report. TL;DR: S4k-v3.2 rollout appears correlated with p95 regression on MidCity's workload. They are a reserved/enterprise account (MID-4721) with a contractual p95 of 800ms.

Proposed immediate actions (please respond with approvals/edits):
1) Activate fallback gating: route MidCity to s4k-v3.2-q (quantized variant) when observed p95 > 1.2s; auto-revert after 2 hours of stable p95 < 900ms.
2) Offer a provisional SLA relief window (carveout) of up to 48 hours while we investigate, with daily status updates and a formal postmortem due in 5 business days.
3) If fallback causes accuracy regressions beyond agreed thresholds, instead apply a 30% traffic cap and prioritize critical flows.
4) Open JIRA-INC-8893 and run the s4k fallback playbook (see attachment).

Attachments: s4k-fallback-playbook.pdf (runbook)

Sam — I'll keep you updated. Ben/Laura/Neha please confirm approvals and any changes to offer terms (credits, duration).

On Sat, Aug 8, 2026 at 4:18 PM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Also noting quality risk: some of MidCity's prompts are very sensitive to tokenization changes; we should include a short A/B check before switching fully to the quantized variant for 100% traffic. Consider a 10% canary for 30 min.

Agree with Ben. A few technical clarifications from SRE/model-onboarding side:
- Root cause hypothesis: a kernel selection path for long-sequence attention in S4k-v3.2 is causing large variance under MidCity's median sequence length (they have a heavy tail of ~1024 tokens). We saw similar tokenslice thrash in internal perf tests when batch size and KV cache patterns align badly.
- Risk of switching to s4k-v3.2-q: slight EM/perplexity regression (~1.6% on our eval set). For MidCity's regulated flows we should validate for top-1 label drift on a held prompt set (we can run that in parallel and report within 2 hours).
- Recommended immediate plan:
  a) 10% canary to s4k-v3.2-q for 30 minutes with A/B checks against a 50-item prompt set.
  b) If canary reduces p95 below 1.2s and passes drift checks (top-1 change <2%), expand to 100% and notify customer.
  c) If canary fails either metric, apply 30% traffic cap and escalate to R&D for kernel rollback.

I'll trigger the canary and start the quick drift evaluation now. Opening JIRA-INC-8893 and will attach results.

- Neha
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
